adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] config/locales/server.en.yml:1852 — `unsubscribe_link` now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`, but only `send_notification_email` passes that key; every other `add_unsubscribe_link: true` caller (e.g. the digest mailer via `MessageBuilder#body` and `#html_part`) will raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` and fail to send

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `config/locales/server.en.yml` `unsubscribe_link` to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}`. In `lib/email/message_builder.rb#html_part`, when `@opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is true it always does `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)`; `template_args` only has defaults for `site_name`, `base_url`, and `user_preferences_url`, and will raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` if `unsubscribe_url` is not present. This diff only adds `unsubscribe_url` in `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` and updates one spec; no default is provided in `MessageBuilder`, so any other existing `add_unsubscribe_link: true` usage without `unsubscribe_url` would break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/security] app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:98 — state-changing action on a GET route with `check_xhr` skipped has no CSRF protection; any page can embed `` to silently mute or un-watch topics for logged-in visitors

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, which mutates `TopicUser.notification_level` and calls `tu.save!` (state change). It is wired up via `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` / `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` in `config/routes.rb`, and `check_xhr` is explicitly skipped for `:unsubscribe` (`skip_before_filter :check_xhr, only: [:show, :unsubscribe, :feed]`). Because this is a state-changing GET endpoint, it can be triggered cross-site (e.g., an embedded ``), and Rails' CSRF protections generally do not apply to GET requests, so the finding’s CSRF/CSRF-like risk is directly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107 — the action is a non-idempotent toggle on a GET; a refresh, back/forward re-fetch, or second click on the email link steps the user from watching to regular to muted with no indication

adjudication.rationale:
In the new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action, the routes added in `config/routes.rb` are `get ... => "topics#unsubscribe"`, but the action performs a state-changing toggle on `TopicUser.notification_level`:
```rb
if tu.notification_level > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]
  tu.notification_level = TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]
else
  tu.notification_level = TopicUser.notification_levels[:muted]
end
```
Because it is triggered via GET (e.g., email link uses `post.topic.unsubscribe_url`), repeating the request (refresh/back-forward/second click) will flip the state again, making the operation non-idempotent and potentially moving users through multiple notification states with no explicit confirmation of the prior state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:113 — writes `notification_level` via `save!` instead of `TopicUser.change`, so `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` are not recorded and the `/topic/:id` MessageBus `notification_level_change` event is not published, leaving open tabs stale and losing audit info

adjudication.rationale: In the new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action, the code updates `tu.notification_level` and persists with `tu.save!` rather than using `TopicUser.change(...)` (which in this diff is shown to `MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", { notification_level_change: ... }, user_ids: [...])` when `attrs[:notification_level]` is set). Because `save!` bypasses that path, the `notification_level_change` MessageBus event will not be published, so any clients relying on that event can remain stale. The additional claims about `notifications_changed_at` / `notifications_reason_id` aren’t directly verifiable from this diff, but the missing MessageBus publish is.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:4 — the Ember route only loads the topic; the mutation happens only on a full-page server request, so entering via client-side transition shows the 'You will stop receiving notifications' message without changing anything

adjudication.rationale: The new Ember route `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6` only loads the topic via `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)` and never calls the Rails `TopicsController#unsubscribe` endpoint that performs the notification level toggle (`tu.notification_level = ...; tu.save!`). Therefore, if the user reaches `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` via an in-app/client-side transition, they’ll see the unsubscribe UI/message (`templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs` rendering `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}`) without any server-side mutation happening.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] config/locales/client.en.yml:985 — confirmation text unconditionally says notifications stop, but when the user was watching/tracking the controller only downgrades to regular, so reply, mention and quote emails continue; the message is wrong for the most common starting state

adjudication.rationale: The new client string `topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications` says the user "will stop receiving notifications" for the topic, but `TopicsController#unsubscribe` does not always stop notifications: it only sets `tu.notification_level` to `:regular` when the user was previously `> :regular` (e.g., tracking/watching), and only mutes when already `<= :regular`. So in a common path (watching/tracking) the user is downgraded, not fully unsubscribed/muted, making the confirmation text misleading/inaccurate relative to the implemented behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/api] config/routes.rb:440 — the email link requires an authenticated session (`ensure_logged_in`), but recipients opening from a mail client are often logged out; `Discourse::NotLoggedIn` on GET redirects to `/` with no explanation or return-to, so the unsubscribe silently fails; email unsubscribe links normally carry a per-user token

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an email-level unsubscribe link that points to `Topic#unsubscribe_url` (e.g. `/t/:topic_id/unsubscribe`) via `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url` in `user_notifications.rb` and the server locale text. The new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action then depends on `current_user` (e.g. `TopicView.new(..., current_user)` and `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, ...)`) and mutates that user’s `TopicUser` record. There is no per-user token in the link and nothing in the diff to make the action work without an authenticated session; if the recipient is logged out, this route cannot safely identify a user and will error or be blocked by auth filters, so the emailed unsubscribe link will not reliably work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb:171 — no test covers the new `unsubscribe` controller action (toggle semantics, missing `TopicUser` row, slug redirect, anonymous access), and the builder spec only adds the new argument without asserting the per-topic link renders or that callers omitting `unsubscribe_url` still work

adjudication.rationale: The new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action dereferences `current_user.id` and `tu.notification_level` without guarding against `current_user` being nil or `TopicUser.find_by(...)` returning nil. In the diff: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` followed by `if tu.notification_level > ...` will raise if no TopicUser row exists (or if current_user is absent). This is a concrete correctness issue introduced by the new action; the finding’s mention of missing coverage for these cases aligns with an actual bug visible in the code.
